authors: A. J. Ellis, R. M. Golding
title: The solubility of carbon dioxide above 100 C in water and in sodium chloride solutions
experimental_method: (1) Liquid analysis: CO2 over water or 0.5, 1, 2 molal NaCl in a ~100 cc vessel equilibrated at least 24 h; ~2 g liquid sampled through a capillary into a weighed water trap and anhydrone/Carbosorb tubes (CO2 swept with N2); CO2 partial pressure = total pressure minus water (Raoult-corrected) vapour pressure. (2) pvt method: water injected into a vessel pre-charged with CO2 at T; condensation and fill points from P vs injected water give vapour and liquid water densities and the Ostwald coefficient.
uncertainties_stated: Volume meter 0.05 percent; vessel temperature ends within +-1 C of centre; steam densities unlikely better than +-5 percent; highest-T solubilities in 2 m NaCl may be low by 5-10 percent (water vapour pressure uncertainty); lambda from the two methods differs by up to 0.05 at 300 C.
quality_remarks: K values (Table 2) are calculated with literature fugacity coefficients (Majumdar and Roy 1956) and lambda with literature CO2 z values (Sweigert et al. 1946) and the Table 1 interpolated densities. Water vapour pressures of NaCl solutions estimated by Raoult's law (authors note it overcorrects at high T, so 2 m runs kept near or below 300 C). Earlier Ellis (1959a) K values corrected (Table 6). Table 3 text mentions 'CO2-H2' (misprint for CO2-H2O). Temperature scale not stated.
